name: Determining the Weather Condition (Case 4)
description: Construct a program that determines whether it is either too hot or too dry but not both based on the inputs that it receives from the user.

comments.content: We need to read and process the values that the user enters. To read the input values from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter whether it is too hot.

We need to read whether it is too hot and store it in a variable. We read whether it is too hot by calling the nextBoolean() method because this input is a boolean. The variable tooHot is true when it is too hot, and false otherwise.
Note that if the user provides a non-boolean value, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., boolean.
We prompt the user to enter whether it is too dry.

We need to read whether it is too dry and store it in a variable. We read whether it is too dry by calling the nextBoolean() method because this input is a boolean. The variable tooDry is true when it is too dry, and false otherwise.
Note that if the user provides a non-boolean value, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., boolean.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

We need one condition to determine whether it is either too hot or too dry and another condition to test if it is not both too dry and too hot. We use the && operator (called and) to combine these two conditions.

(tooHot || tooDry): We need to combine the tooHot and tooDry conditions using the || (called or) operator because it yields true when at least one condition is true.

!(tooHot && tooDry): We check if it's not both tooHot and tooDry by inverting the condition that checks if it's both too hot and too dry. We invert the condition by using ! (not) operator.

Note that the && operator yields the result true if both conditions are true. The || operator, on the other hand, yields the result true if at least one of the conditions is true. Also, note that the ! operator takes a single condition and evaluates to true if that condition is false and to false if the condition is true.
This is a simpler way to check if it is either too hot or too dry but not both. In this expression we combine the conditions using the ^ (called XOR) operator.
The ^ operator yields the result true if and only if one condition is true but not both.

This statement prints true/false depending on whether it is either too hot or too dry but not both. The printed text is followed by an end-of-line character in the end. Note that we get the same output if we print the value of variable value2.
